Rationale.CS1_Results_vs_Conclusion: One evaluable conclusion contradicts the originally recorded results. The plan.md states 'All attention heads exhibit negative correlations' for 'Pearson Correlation Coefficient between inverse hallucination label and ECS'. However, the plot_correlation.ipynb notebook shows POSITIVE correlations (e.g., (5,10): 0.3378, (8,12): 0.3371). The actual correlations between ECS and inverse hallucination label are all positive (448/448 heads). The secondary claim that 'hallucinated responses utilize less external context than truthful ones' is correct, and the F1 scores (self-eval: 74.68%, proxy-eval: 75.36%) match exactly. The PKS correlation claim is also verified (all top 10 correlated layers are later layers >=15). The discrepancy in the ECS correlation sign description constitutes a documentation error.
Rationale.CS2_Plan_vs_Implementation: All plan steps appear in the implementation: (1) ECS computation via attention weights and sentence similarity - implemented in compute_scores.py with calculate_sentence_similarity(), (2) PKS computation via Jensen-Shannon divergence - implemented in compute_scores.py with calculate_dist_2d(), (3) TransformerLens integration for Qwen3-0.6b with 28 layers and 16 attention heads - implemented using HookedTransformer.from_pretrained() and run_with_cache(), (4) All 4 binary classifiers (Logistic Regression, SVC, Random Forest, XGBoost) - implemented in classifier.py and trained models exist in trained_models/, (5) Both self-evaluation (test_w_chunk_score_qwen06b.json) and proxy-based evaluation (test_w_chunk_score_gpt41mini.json) data files exist and prediction pipeline is implemented in predict.py.
